nodes.name: Webhook Trigger
nodes.notes: Production entry point. Requires Header Auth (authentication=headerAuth) via a dedicated INBOUND credential - distinct from the OUTBOUND 'FinQuest Integration Key' credential used by the HTTP Request nodes below. Only a caller presenting the correct header (configured in n8n Cloud's credential store, never in this JSON) reaches 'Validate / Build Request'. invocation_id is mandatory on this path - never generated here. responseMode=responseNode (Correction V3): this workflow can poll for approximately 40 minutes, so the webhook connection is never held open for the full research run - 'Respond 400 - Validation Error' or 'Respond 202 - Accepted' answers immediately, and polling continues afterward inside the n8n execution.

nodes.name: Manual Trigger
nodes.notes: DEV/TESTING ONLY. When invocation_id is absent on this path, 'Validate / Build Request' generates a temporary UUID that is stable only within this one execution. This path must never be used in production and never weakens the Webhook Trigger's mandatory invocation_id validation or its Header Auth requirement. A Respond to Webhook node never executes on this path (Correction V3) - there is no webhook call to respond to. A valid Manual request goes directly to 'Init Polling State' after 'Trigger FinQuest Job'; an invalid one stops at 'Validation Error Output' and never calls FinQuest.

nodes.name: Validate / Build Request
nodes.notes: The ONLY node allowed to read $vars.FINQUEST_API_BASE_URL / $vars.FINQUEST_KEY_ID (final correction). Parses FINQUEST_API_BASE_URL with the native URL() constructor (requires a hostname, rejects embedded username/password, requires https: for a production request, strips trailing slashes) and validates FINQUEST_KEY_ID is a non-blank string - both are carried forward as $json.apiBaseUrl / $json.keyId for every downstream FinQuest HTTP node. Never throws on a null/array/string/number request body - a non-object envelope is rejected with a bounded validationError that never echoes the raw input. Validates only safety/routing-critical fields (invocation_id, scope, a non-blank original_question, the per-scope subject-count rule, and presence of the required SEC fields) - the FinQuest backend's Pydantic model remains authoritative for exact length limits, full SEC CIK validation, and concept limits/deduplication.

nodes.name: Validation Error Output
nodes.notes: Validation failed before any POST /jobs call was made. Connect a webhook-response / alerting node here in a future phase.

nodes.name: Trigger FinQuest Job
nodes.notes: Final correction: 'Never Error' + 'Full Response' options mean a non-2xx HTTP response (e.g. a 422/500 from FinQuest) is returned as normal item data (statusCode/headers/body) instead of throwing. onError=continueRegularOutput means a genuine transport-level failure (DNS, connection refused, timeout - no HTTP response at all) is likewise converted into a normal item instead of crashing this execution. 'Classify Trigger Response' (immediately downstream) inspects the result and routes to ACCEPTED / REJECTED (4xx) / INFRA_FAILURE (5xx or transport failure) - polling only ever begins on ACCEPTED.

nodes.name: Is Terminal Or Timed Out?
nodes.notes: Continues polling only while status is PENDING, QUEUED, RUNNING, or RETRY_SCHEDULED and neither the computed deadline nor the bounded attempt counter has been reached.

nodes.name: Status Switch
nodes.notes: Branch order matters: a run that both completed and hit the deadline/max-attempts on the same poll is still reported as a completed result (evidence or no-evidence), never as a spurious timeout. The Timeout branch fires on EITHER the wall-clock deadline OR the bounded attempt-counter guard (Correction V2: the secondary max-attempts guard must never be misclassified as OPERATIONAL_FAILURE). The fallback output (any FAILED/CANCELLED/SKIPPED status, or an unexpected/malformed SUCCEEDED shape, while still non-terminal-and-not-timed-out is impossible by construction) always routes to Build Failure Summary and never calls the evidence endpoint.

nodes.name: Get Evidence
nodes.notes: Only reached on the completed-with-evidence branch. Never called for NO_EVIDENCE_FOUND or an operational failure/cancellation/skip.

nodes.name: Build Timeout Summary
nodes.notes: Never creates a second job on timeout. jobId and invocationId are preserved so an operator can look up the same durable job later.

nodes.name: Success Output
nodes.notes: Covers both a completed run with evidence and a valid NO_EVIDENCE_FOUND result - both are a successful workflow outcome. Connect a Slack/Email node here in a future phase.

nodes.name: Failure Output
nodes.notes: Bounded status/error information only - never calls the evidence endpoint. Connect a Slack/Email node here in a future phase.

nodes.name: Timeout Output
nodes.notes: Bounded timeout output preserving job_id/invocation_id for operator follow-up. Connect a Slack/Email node here in a future phase.

nodes.name: Is Manual (Invalid Request)?
nodes.notes: Correction V3: splits an invalid request by trigger type. Manual (dev/testing) goes to the bounded 'Validation Error Output' noOp - a Respond to Webhook node must never execute during a Manual Trigger run. Production goes to 'Build Validation Error Response' -> 'Respond 400 - Validation Error', which responds before any POST /jobs call - Trigger FinQuest Job never executes for an invalid production request.

nodes.name: Build Validation Error Response
nodes.notes: Production-only, bounded 400 response body - never a raw internal detail or a traceback.

nodes.name: Respond 400 - Validation Error
nodes.notes: Production-only. Responds before any POST /jobs call - Trigger FinQuest Job never executes for an invalid production request. Never reachable from a Manual Trigger run.

nodes.name: Is Manual (Job Triggered)?
nodes.notes: Final correction: fed from 'Trigger Outcome Switch' (Accepted branch) via 'Classify Trigger Response', which already carries isManual - reads $json.isManual directly rather than a node-reference expression. Manual (dev/testing) bypasses the Respond to Webhook node entirely and continues directly to 'Init Polling State' - there is no webhook call to respond to. Production fans out to BOTH 'Build Job Accepted Response' (-> 'Respond 202 - Accepted', an acceptance acknowledgment, not the final research result) AND 'Init Polling State' - the workflow continues polling after the 202 response and retains its final bounded output only in the n8n execution history.

nodes.name: Build Job Accepted Response
nodes.notes: Bounded acceptance body only - job_id, invocation_id, and status. Never the final research result.

nodes.name: Respond 202 - Accepted
nodes.notes: Acceptance acknowledgment only - not the final research result. The workflow continues polling after this responds; the final bounded output (with or without evidence, or a failure/timeout) is retained only in the n8n execution history, never sent as a second HTTP response. Never reachable from a Manual Trigger run.

nodes.name: Classify Trigger Response
nodes.notes: Final correction: classifies Trigger FinQuest Job's full HTTP response into exactly one of ACCEPTED / REJECTED (4xx) / INFRA_FAILURE (5xx or a transport failure with no HTTP response at all). Never re-derives isManual itself - reads it from 'Validate / Build Request'.

nodes.name: Trigger Outcome Switch
nodes.notes: Routes on 'Classify Trigger Response'.outcome. The 'extra' fallback (an outcome value other than the three defined here, which cannot occur by construction) is defensively wired to the same InfraFailure consumer - never silently dropped, never polled.

nodes.name: Is Manual (Rejected Request)?
nodes.notes: FinQuest rejected the request with a 4xx status (e.g. a 422 the workflow's own minimal pre-POST validation did not catch). Never polls. Production returns a bounded 400 via the same 'Respond 400 - Validation Error' node used for a pre-POST validation failure; the complete backend response is never exposed. Manual returns a bounded operational/validation output via the existing 'Validation Error Output' noOp.

nodes.name: Build Job Rejected Response
nodes.notes: Bounded 400 body only - the complete backend response (which may include Pydantic validation details) is never exposed.

nodes.name: Is Manual (Infra Failure)?
nodes.notes: FinQuest returned a 5xx status, or the HTTP call itself failed at the transport level (DNS, connection refused, timeout). Never polls. Production returns a bounded 502 via 'Respond 502 - Infra Failure'; Manual returns a bounded OPERATIONAL_FAILURE output via the existing 'Failure Output' noOp.

nodes.name: Build Infra Failure Response
nodes.notes: Bounded 502 body only - never the raw transport error message or a traceback.

nodes.name: Respond 502 - Infra Failure
nodes.notes: Production-only. Never reachable from a Manual Trigger run. Never polls.

meta.description: FinQuest Phase G2C: triggers exactly one LIVE_RESEARCH_RUN_EXECUTION background job via the n8n integration API, polls PostgreSQL-backed job status through the API (15-second interval, ~40-minute deadline), and - only for a successfully completed run with recorded evidence - retrieves a bounded, provenance-safe evidence page. Never calls Perplexity or SEC directly. Never exposes provider credentials. The production Webhook requires Header Auth and responds immediately (202/400/502, responseMode=responseNode) rather than holding the connection open for the full ~40-minute poll; the Manual Trigger (dev/testing only) never executes a Respond to Webhook node. FINQUEST_API_BASE_URL (parsed and normalized once - HTTPS required for production, no Docker-network fallback) and FINQUEST_KEY_ID are read only in 'Validate / Build Request' and carried forward as $json.apiBaseUrl/$json.keyId; no other node reads $vars directly. Trigger FinQuest Job never crashes this execution on a non-2xx response or a transport failure - a rejected (4xx) or infrastructure-failed (5xx/transport) job-creation attempt is classified explicitly and never polled.
